contentBlocks.text: You already know your own community well — your neighborhood, your town, the people around you. This week we'll travel the world (without leaving home!) to explore communities very different from your own.

Every community shares three things in common: people who live and work together, an environment (the land, weather, and natural surroundings), and traditions (the shared customs, celebrations, and ways of doing things passed down over time). Think about your own community: Who are the people you see often? What is the environment like — is it hilly, flat, near water, hot, or cold? What's one tradition or celebration your community shares? Write down one example of each.
You just described your own community using the same three ideas — people, environment, and traditions — that we'll use all week to explore communities around the world.

objectives: Identify the three shared elements of any community: people, environment, and traditions
Describe their own community using these three elements
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child to describe their own community in their own words first.
2. Introduce the three-part framework: people, environment, traditions.
3. Walk through each element using their own community as the example.
4. Complete the worksheet, describing their own community's people/environment/traditions.
5. Preview that this week explores communities very different from their own, starting with a real region called Punjab.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use very concrete prompts (What's the weather like today? What holiday did you celebrate most recently?) rather than abstract ones
Ready for more: ask them to compare their own community to a grandparent's or relative's community if they have one in a different place
This lesson works well paired with a family photo or a walk around the neighborhood if possible
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary based on the child's own community — check that each answer genuinely reflects the category (people/environment/traditions), not a repeat of the same idea three times.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Grounds the C3 Framework's Geography and Culture dimensions in the child's own lived experience before comparing to an unfamiliar community — matching the course's own 'world communities and cultures' description.

generationData.instructions: Respond to each prompt in complete sentences.

prompts.prompt: Describe the people in your community.
Describe the environment (land, weather) where you live.
Describe one tradition or celebration your community shares.
